terms.gloss: as (a boy, an old man): the noun beside its subject, in the same case
terms.grammar: construction: no word for “as”; the noun agrees with the person in case
evidence: Cic. Sen. 10: senem adulēscēns ita dīlēxī
Cic. Sen. 26: litterās Graecās senex didicī
terms.comment: “I learned Greek as an old man” is litterās Graecās senex didicī. “When I was a boy” can also be the ablative absolute mē puerō.

evidence: Sen. Ep. 87.3: prō pulmentāriō sunt … prō pāne
terms.comment: What a person or thing is taken for or serves as; and in titles of office held in another’s place: prō cōnsule, as proconsul. For “in place of”, locō with the genitive (see instead).

phrases.latin: ego Q. Maximum, eum quī Tarentum recēpit, senem adulēscēns ita dīlēxī, ut aequālem
phrases.english: Quintus Maximus, the man who recovered Tarentum, I loved as a young man, old as he was, as if he were my own age

phrases.latin: et ego fēcī quī litterās Graecās senex didicī
phrases.english: and so did I, who learned Greek as an old man

phrases.latin: ēditus in lūcem jacuit sine vīribus īnfāns; mox quadrupēs rītūque tulit sua membra ferārum
phrases.english: brought into the light, he lay there as a baby without strength; soon he moved his limbs on all fours, the way animals do
when I was a boy, as I remember

phrases.latin: nusquam sine cāricīs, numquam sine pugillāribus; illae, sī pānem habeō, prō pulmentāriō sunt, sī nōn habeō, prō pāne
phrases.english: never anywhere without dried figs, never without my notebooks: the figs serve as a relish if I have bread, and as bread if I have none

phrases.latin: cum prō cōnsule in Ciliciam proficīscēns vēnissem Athēnās
phrases.english: when I had come to Athens on my way to Cilicia as proconsul
